questions.q: What is the precise difference between a metaphor and a simile? Give one example of each from everyday Hindi usage.
questions.a: A metaphor directly equates two things (e.g., "समय धन है" — Time is money), while a simile uses "जैसा" or "सा" to compare (e.g., "वह शेर जैसा बहादुर है" — He is brave like a lion). A wrong answer that says "both compare things" reveals the student has not grasped the structural distinction that metaphor asserts identity, which is crucial for analyzing Prasad's dense metaphorical statements like "जीवन एक प्रवाह है".

questions.q: In the poem "olar vk;k", the line "बड़े-बड़े फूल, ऊँचे ऊँचे पेड़" creates a visual image. Explain how this image contributes to the poem's mood *before* the speaker realizes the fleeting nature of the scene.
questions.a: The image establishes a mood of grandeur, permanence, and overwhelming beauty — tall trees and large flowers suggest a world that is majestic and enduring. This sets up the sharp contrast when the speaker later realizes "हम फँसते जाते हैं" (we keep getting trapped). A student who only says "it shows nature is beautiful" misses the structural role of the image in creating a false sense of stability that the poem later shatters.

questions.q: Identify one metaphor in "rksM+ks" that compares an abstract concept to a concrete object. Write the line (by description, not full quote) and explain the comparison.
questions.a: The metaphor "हृदय की आँच" (the heart's heat/flame) compares emotional passion or life-force to a physical fire. The concrete object (fire/heat) makes the abstract feeling tangible, suggesting it can be fanned, can burn, and can also die out. A wrong answer that picks "पत्थर" (stone) as a metaphor for "heart" without explaining the *comparative* logic shows the student is confusing a symbol with a metaphor.

questions.q: Compare the use of auditory imagery in the two poems. How does the sound imagery in "olar vk;k" (e.g., the description of the bird's call) differ in function from the sound imagery in "rksM+ks" (e.g., the repeated "रक्से रक्से")?
questions.a: In "olar vk;k", the bird's call ("फिर फिर फिर") mimics the repetitive, cyclical nature of time and memory, pulling the speaker back to the past. In "rksM+ks", the onomatopoeic "रक्से रक्से" (the sound of chiseling/hammering) creates a rhythmic, almost musical insistence that mirrors the persistent, laborious effort to carve a path through stone. A student who merely lists the sounds without linking them to the poems' respective themes (nostalgia vs. determined action) has not analyzed the functional difference.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "The metaphor of 'पत्थर' (stone) in 'rksM+ks' is more effective than the metaphor of 'प्रवाह' (flow) in 'olar vk;k' because it is more concrete." Defend or refute with evidence from the poems.
questions.a: Refute. Effectiveness depends on thematic fit, not concreteness alone. "पत्थर" brilliantly embodies the obstinate resistance of circumstance and the hardness of the path, while "प्रवाह" perfectly captures the relentless, uncontrollable, and transient nature of time and life. Both are equally effective *for their respective poems*. A student who agrees with the claim reveals a misconception that "concrete = better" and fails to see that metaphors serve specific thematic purposes.

questions.q: Create a four-line Hindi poem stanza that uses at least two different types of sensory imagery (e.g., visual + olfactory) and one metaphor to express the feeling of waiting for exam results.
questions.a:
Example:
"कमरे में धुएँ-सी घुलती चिंता की गंध, (olfactory)
दीवार पर टिकी घड़ी की टिक-टिक, (auditory)
भविष्य एक बंद दरवाज़ा, चाबी खोई कहीं, (metaphor)
साँस रोककर बैठा हूँ, परिणाम की प्रतीक्षा में।" (tactile/kinesthetic)
A poor answer that uses only visual imagery ("मैं खिड़की से देखता हूँ") and no metaphor shows the student cannot yet synthesize the devices creatively.
